rules.name: checkApprovalCeiling
rules.statement: A value above the role's ceiling must escalate rather than be approved.
messages: This role may not approve.
${formatSar(amountHalalas)} is above this role

rules.name: checkQcIndependence
rules.statement: A technician cannot pass QC on a repair they performed.
messages: The technician who performed the repair cannot pass its quality check.

rules.name: checkSelfApproval
rules.statement: The approver must not be the submitter — the first and most-broken SOD pair, and the one that lets a single person move money on their own say-so.
messages: The person who raised this cannot also approve it.

rules.name: SOD_PAIRS
rules.statement: The declared conflicting-duty pairs, exposed so a screen can explain one.

rules.name: payrollLineNetHalalas
rules.statement: A payroll line's net pay: earnings plus allowances, less deductions. Every input is integer halalas, so the result is too — no rounding, no float.

rules.name: checkMovement
rules.statement: No negative stock unless the part is explicitly backorderable, and never a consumption larger than what is unreserved — unless it consumes a reservation, in which case the reservation is the bound.
messages: A movement quantity must be positive.
Cannot consume more than is reserved.
This movement would take stock negative and the part is not backorderable.
Only unreserved stock can be consumed or transferred.

rules.name: checkReceipt
rules.statement: Receiving quantity ≤ ordered quantity; over-receipt needs approval.
messages: Receiving more than was ordered needs an approval.

rules.name: checkReservation
rules.statement: `Reserved ≤ Available`.
messages: Cannot reserve more than is on hand.

rules.name: checkReservationRelease
rules.statement: A release cannot give back more than is held.
messages: Cannot release more than is reserved.

rules.name: movementDelta
rules.statement: The sign a movement type applies to on-hand quantity. For a transfer this is the sign of the *debit* row. The route writes the paired credit row (+qty against the destination branch) in the same transaction, so the org's books conserve; this function answers "what does the requested row do", which is also the feasibility question the guard below asks.

rules.name: amortisedInstalmentHalalas
rules.statement: The level monthly instalment that amortises `principalHalalas` over `termMonths` at `rateBps` annual, as an integer count of halalas. A zero-rate loan divides the principal evenly, rounded half-up; the schedule then absorbs any remainder in the final instalment. Otherwise the standard annuity formula `P·i / (1 − (1+i)^−n)` gives the payment, with `i` the monthly rate. The `Math.pow` is the one floating-point step, and its product with the principal is rounded to a whole halala before it is ever used — nothing fractional is returned or stored.

rules.name: buildRepaymentPlan
rules.statement: The full amortised schedule for a loan. Each month: interest is computed on the running balance in integer halalas, the principal portion is the instalment minus that interest, and the balance is reduced by the principal portion. The final instalment is set to clear the balance exactly (`balance + interest`), so the amounts collect precisely `principalHalalas + Σ interest` with no drift, and no instalment ever amortises more principal than remains.

rules.name: monthlyInterestHalalas
rules.statement: One month's interest on an outstanding balance, in integer halalas: `balance · rateBps / (10000 · 12)`, rounded half-up at the last halala.

rules.name: checkJournalBalanced
rules.statement: Double-entry: debits must equal credits.
messages: A journal entry needs at least two lines.
Journal entry debits must equal credits.

rules.name: checkPayment
rules.statement: `Payment.amount ≤ invoice.balance`, and a cancelled invoice takes none.
messages: A cancelled invoice cannot take a payment.
An invoice must be issued before it can take a payment.
A payment must be greater than zero.
A payment cannot exceed the outstanding balance.

rules.name: checkRefund
rules.statement: `Refund ≤ amount collected`.
messages: A refund cannot exceed the amount collected.

rules.name: computeInvoiceTotals
rules.statement: `total = subtotal + tax − discount`, with tax computed on the discounted net. Rounding happens at the subtotal and at the tax, not on every line, so a 500-line invoice does not drift by 500 halalas.

rules.name: roundHalfUp
rules.statement: Half-up rounding at the last halala, applied once — never per line.

rules.name: VAT_RATE_BPS
rules.statement: ZATCA standard rate. Stored as basis points so the rate itself is exact.

rules.name: checkPurchaseOrderApprovable
rules.statement: A purchase order may only be approved while it is a draft.
messages: This purchase order is already approved.
A ${status} purchase order can no longer be approved.

rules.name: checkReceive
rules.statement: Receiving quantity ≤ ordered quantity (§5b). An over-receipt is never returned as `ok`: the caller must refuse it or route it to approval.
messages: Receive a positive whole number of units.
Receiving ${incomingQty} takes this line to ${after} of ${orderedQty} ordered — ${

rules.name: purchaseOrderTotals
rules.statement: `subtotal + VAT`, summed from the lines by the server. Never sent by the client — a purchase order's total is decided here.

rules.name: requisitionEstimatedTotalHalalas
rules.statement: The VAT-exclusive estimated value of a requisition's lines.

rules.name: checkBayFree
messages: ${candidate.bay} is already booked for that time.

rules.name: checkEstimateFresh
rules.statement: An expired estimate cannot be approved.
messages: This estimate has expired and cannot be approved.

rules.name: checkInvoiceable
rules.statement: A completed job card is required before invoicing.
messages: A job must reach delivery before it can be invoiced.

rules.name: checkStageTransition
rules.statement: A stage gate cannot be skipped.
messages: The job is already at ${to}.
A job at ${from} cannot move to ${to}.

rules.name: overlaps
rules.statement: An appointment cannot double-book a bay. Half-open intervals, so a job ending at 10:30 and one starting at 10:30 do not collide.
